description: A customer has reported that date-range exports show incorrect revenue totals for Q1 2024 (Jan 1 - Mar 31). The support team has escalated this with ticket #2847 and sample data. Your task: (1) Read the support ticket at 'support_ticket_2847.txt' in the workspace to understand the issue - customer expects $52,150 but sees $45,230 for Q1 2024 date range. (2) Examine 'customer_data_sample.csv' to see the transaction data format. (3) Navigate the codebase in the 'src/' directory to find where date filtering happens - use Ctrl+Shift+F to search for 'filter' or 'date_range', or explore files manually. The bug is in 'src/date_utils.py' in the 'filter_by_date_range' function. (4) Identify the specific bug: the line 'if start <= txn_date < end:' uses '<' instead of '<=' for the end date, making it exclusive instead of inclusive as documented. This causes transactions on the last day (March 31) to be excluded. (5) Document your findings by adding a comment within 5 lines of the buggy comparison line. Your comment MUST include: a marker like TODO, FIXME, BUG, or XXX; mention this is a bug/error/problem; explain the technical issue (end date is exclusive instead of inclusive, off-by-one error); describe the impact (transactions on last day excluded, causing wrong totals). Example good comment: '# TODO: BUG #2847 - Off-by-one error: end date comparison uses < instead of <=, making end_date exclusive when documentation promises inclusive range. This excludes transactions on the last day (e.g., March 31), causing incorrect export totals.' Save the file when done (Ctrl+S). Workspace location: /home/ga/workspace/analytics_app/
